Research result

Yes, this is a workable way to test.

Amazon explicitly supports sharing a storefront or affiliate product links through social content. Casey can use image posts to send people to Amazon; the post does not need to be a video review. Amazon’s explanation ↗

The commission comes from a qualifying purchase through Casey’s earning link—not from the image, a Facebook like, or the click alone.Amazon Associates offsite linking is the model for this test. Account terms and purchase eligibility still apply. Operating Agreement ↗

Recommended account setup

A dedicated Page and the spare Instagram.

Use KC’s Finds as the working name. Connect the intended Instagram professional account to the Page for the publishing workflow, and verify both destinations in Meta Business Suite.

Connecting them is an organizational choice. It does not itself guarantee more traffic. Confirm the exact handles and account access during setup.

Keep the production simple

No new AI video project is needed.

Casey’s real review videos can continue as usual. These images are additional promotional posts. We can test the three boards already prepared before creating more.

“Ad” here describes promotional content. The proposed first test uses organic posts, with no paid boosting or new tool purchase.

Facebook Page

Put the earning link in the post text.

A caption structure you can reuse

The bracketed destination is intentionally unfinished. Insert Casey’s generated link before use. This is a promotional concept, not a claim that she has tested every pictured item.

Make the promotion clear

What the post should communicate.

The affiliate relationship

Put a clear commission disclosure with the recommendation, where readers will see it before following the link. Add the required account statement in a visible profile/About location: “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.” The profile statement does not replace a disclosure in the post. Amazon guidance ↗

The image is a promotional concept

Review generated product details against the actual listing. Avoid invented performance claims, inaccurate pack sizes, or imagery that suggests Casey personally used an item when she did not. A disclosure does not repair a misleading product depiction. FTC guidance requires truthful endorsements and real experience for experience claims. FTC guidance ↗

What the customer will find after clicking

Use one clear instruction: “Shop this product,” “Browse Family Fun Finds,” or “Find this collection through my profile link.” Keep the linked item or list consistent with the picture. Update the existing boards’ review-gallery footers before publishing them.

Casey’s three posts a week

Prepare once. Publish across the week.

Suggested split: Sofía prepares the batch and links; Casey reviews the products and wording; the agreed publishing owner schedules the approved posts.

MondayFamily finds

A themed board or a product with a clear family use.

First available draft: family activities and gifts.
WednesdayHome finds

A practical grouping tied to one household task.

First available draft: home organization.
FridaySeasonal finds

Products that fit current plans or the coming holiday.

First available draft: fall weekends.

This recurring rhythm is a proposal. The existing launch packet’s first-week dates are October 7, 9 and 12; shift them if setup takes longer. Real review videos can appear between image posts. Choose initial times, then adjust to actual audience data.

One time setup
01

Confirm the accounts.

Create or identify the dedicated Facebook Page. Confirm the spare Instagram handle, professional setup, connection and publishing access in Meta Business Suite.

02

Set up the shopping route.

Make the storefront easy to find from the profiles and organize the relevant collections. Keep the exact new social URLs up to date in the Amazon Associates site list. Amazon site-list steps ↗

Each weekly batch

Schedule in Meta Business Suite.

  1. Select the correct Page and connected Instagram destination.
  2. Create a post, upload the chosen image, and add the caption and disclosure.
  3. Adjust the link instruction for each platform using the Posting guide.
  4. Preview both versions, check the destination, then choose the date and account timezone.
  5. Schedule and confirm the post appears in the planned-content calendar.

Meta’s official tutorial supports this general workflow. Current menus, permissions and supported options must be checked in Casey’s account; they were not inspected here. Meta for Business tutorial ↗

What counts as progress?

Learn whether the posts drive purchases.

QuestionLook atWhat it helps decide
Are people seeing it?Post reach or viewsWhether distribution is sufficient to learn anything.
Are they following the link?Available outbound clicks; Amazon-reported clicksWhether the image, caption and buying path create interest.
Are purchases qualifying?Amazon ordered items and reported commissionsWhether the traffic is producing earnings after reporting settles.
Is the work worth repeating?Results alongside preparation timeWhich topics to repeat, improve or pause.

Use account-generated tracking IDs to compare Facebook and Instagram where supported. A shared storefront URL may not isolate individual posts, and link-service counts may differ from Amazon’s. Check after seven days, then review purchase results after fourteen days; keep observing if traffic is low. Amazon tracking IDs ↗

Where Viral Vue fits

A research aid, not the checkout.

Use the existing product research to help decide what fits Casey’s audience. We do not need a new tool to start this social test: Amazon provides link generation, and Meta provides the scheduling workflow.

The earlier research did not establish a universal conversion advantage for third-party deep links. Test the native buying path first; investigate another route only if the evidence gives us a reason.

The research behind the answer

Sources you can open.

Focused on Casey’s October 5 question about image posts, storefront links, commissions and weekly scheduling. Prepared October 6, 2026, with Amazon.com US as the working market.

What is verified and what is proposed

Amazon documents storefront sharing, affiliate link generation, disclosure and tracking. The weekly cadence, themed collections and fourteen-day observation period are recommendations for this test.

Casey’s account settings, specific commission rates, eligibility, final links and earnings have not been audited. Meta help access was limited; its older official tutorial supports the general scheduling process. Confirm the live controls during setup. This report does not establish blanket platform approval for every AI-generated image.

The report is a saved snapshot. It does not update automatically, access accounts, send messages or schedule posts. Product and campaign availability need checking before use.
